data.why: The repo ships 12 built-in demo datasets with matching plain-English questions in data/demo/demos.json, selectable directly in the UI's 'Demo dataset' radio button, which is the primary way to exercise every goal below; one small cross-sectional demo (marketing_ab_test.csv, ~170 rows) is also copied into prep/data/ so the browser agent can exercise the 'Upload CSV' path with the matching question from demos.json ('We ran an A/B test with free shipping. Did it increase the conversion rate?').

goals: Decide which causal inference method fits a dataset and a plain-English question, and get a stated rationale
Check whether the identifying assumptions for difference-in-differences hold (parallel pre-trends) before trusting a DiD estimate
Check instrument strength and exclusion-restriction plausibility when an instrumental-variable design is suggested
Detect poor covariate overlap between treated and control units and get an alternative (trimmed AIPW or matching) instead of a silently extrapolated regression
Get an honest refusal with an explanation of what additional data (an instrument, a mediator, a control group) would be needed when the question is not identifiable from the uploaded data
Compare a classical-ML baseline recommendation against the from-scratch CausalGPT-mini model's recommendation for the same question

review.summary: The tree is accurate and well evidenced for the one path it explored: Prop 99 → options → mark a hidden confounder → recommendation. It shows the core loop of asking, reading the advice, checking the assumptions and re-running. It misses most of what the README says makes the tool distinctive (instrument checks, poor overlap leading to options, honest refusals, low-confidence parse warnings, uploading your own CSV), so it needs more runs on the other demos before it is filed.
